issues.legal_issue: A civil court retains jurisdiction to execute an existing ejectment decree against a thika tenant because the statutory requirement to apply to the Controller governs original ejectment proceedings, not execution of a decree already obtained.
material_facts: A landlord obtained an ejectment decree against a thika tenant, and the decree was affirmed on appeal.
The landlord later applied to a civil court to execute the decree and recover possession.
A transitional remedy had been available to the judgment-debtor to challenge the decree, but the judgment-debtor did not pursue it.
The civil courts rejected the objection that only the Controller could entertain the execution application.
issues.conclusion: Section 5(1) did not apply to execution of the existing ejectment decree, and the civil court had jurisdiction to entertain the execution application.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 3 and 5(1) of the Calcutta Thika Tenancy Act, 1949, the Controller's procedure applies when a landlord initiates an original proceeding to eject a thika tenant on a statutory ground; it does not govern a decree-holder seeking execution of an existing decree. The deletion of sections 28 and 29 did not enlarge the Controller's jurisdiction to reopen decrees. The transitional remedy under section 5(2) of the 1952 amending Ordinance, continued by section 9 of the 1953 amending Act, was the available means to challenge decrees in the relevant class; a decree not challenged through that route could be executed under ordinary law. Consistently with Heydon's Case, welfare legislation should receive a beneficent construction where statutory words permit competing constructions, but the Legislature's intention must first be found in the words used, given their plain grammatical meaning where they admit only one construction.

rule.if: is_execution_of_existing_ejectment_decree and decree_from_competent_court and decree_is_final and thika_tenancy_ejectment_law_applies and not original_ejectment_application and transitional_challenge_not_pursued

predicates.is_execution_of_existing_ejectment_decre: A decree-holder seeks through an execution proceeding to enforce an already issued ejectment decree.
predicates.decree_from_competent_court: A court with authority to decide the ejectment claim issued the decree.
predicates.decree_is_final: The ejectment decree remains operative after available challenges to it have failed or have not been pursued.
predicates.thika_tenancy_ejectment_law_applies: The proceeding concerns ejectment of a tenant protected by a statutory tenancy regime.
predicates.original_ejectment_application: The landlord is initiating an original application seeking an order of ejectment rather than enforcing an existing decree.
predicates.transitional_challenge_not_pursued: The judgment-debtor did not use an available transitional procedure to challenge the existing decree.

issues.definition: When a final ejectment decree issued by a competent court concerns a protected tenancy, the landlord is enforcing that decree rather than bringing an original ejectment application, and the judgment-debtor did not pursue an available transitional challenge, a civil court may entertain execution.
